prompt: In Arkansas, a driver age 21 or older can be arrested for driving while intoxicated (DWI) with an alcohol concentration of at least:
explanation: Arkansas arrests drivers for DWI at an alcohol concentration of 0.08% or more in the breath or blood.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 86

prompt: A driver under 21 can be arrested for Underage Driving Under the Influence in Arkansas at an alcohol concentration of:
explanation: Drivers under 21 can be arrested for Underage DUI at 0.02%. It is illegal to buy or drink alcohol under 21 in Arkansas.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 87

prompt: A 20-year-old Arkansas driver is stopped with an alcohol concentration of 0.05%. What applies?
choices: The driver can be arrested for Underage DUI, which starts at 0.02%
Nothing, because the driver is below 0.08%
Only a warning, because it is a first stop
The driver can be charged only if a crash occurred
explanation: For drivers under 21 the limit is 0.02%, so 0.05% is enough for an Underage DUI arrest. The 0.08% limit applies to adults.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 87

prompt: Driving a commercial vehicle in Arkansas is DWI at what alcohol concentration, no matter what class of license the driver holds?
explanation: DWI in a commercial vehicle is charged at an alcohol concentration of 0.04%, regardless of the driver's license class.
ref: Arkansas DFA Office of Driver Services, DUI/DWI Information

prompt: An Arkansas driver with an alcohol concentration of 0.06% causes a traffic crash. According to the Arkansas study guide, the driver:
choices: Cannot be charged with DWI because the level is under 0.08%
Can be charged only if the driver is under 21
Can be charged with DWI, because a crash or serious offense at 0.04%-0.08% can lead to a DWI charge
Will receive only a written warning
explanation: If you are involved in a traffic crash or a serious traffic offense, you can be charged with DWI with an alcohol content between 0.04% and 0.08%.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 86

prompt: In Arkansas, refusing a chemical test for alcohol for the first time results in a license suspension of:
explanation: A first refusal to submit to a chemical test brings a 180-day suspension. A second refusal within 5 years brings a 2-year suspension.
ref: Arkansas DFA Office of Driver Services, Refusals (A.C.A. § 5-65-205)

prompt: Under current Arkansas law, how long is the license suspension for a first DWI (alcohol) offense?
explanation: Arkansas suspends the license for 6 months for a first DWI offense; a second offense within 5 years brings a 24-month suspension.
ref: Arkansas DFA Office of Driver Services, DUI/DWI/BUI/BWI Offenses (A.C.A. § 5-65-104)

prompt: A first DWI conviction in Arkansas carries a fine of:
explanation: A first alcohol conviction brings a fine of $150 to $1,000 plus court costs, and the driver could also be sentenced to up to one year in jail.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 86

prompt: A driver under 21 gets a first Underage DUI in Arkansas. How long is the license suspended?
explanation: A first Underage DUI (or underage refusal) brings a 90-day suspension; a second brings 1 year.
ref: Arkansas DFA Office of Driver Services, Underage Offenses (A.C.A. § 5-65-304)

prompt: Under Arkansas law, where may an open container of alcohol be kept in a car that has a trunk?
choices: In a cup holder, if the driver is not drinking
On the back seat, if a passenger holds it
explanation: An open alcoholic beverage container may not be in the seating area or anywhere the driver or a passenger can easily reach. The trunk (or a locked glove box or console) is allowed.
ref: Arkansas Code Annotated, A.C.A. § 5-71-218

prompt: Which Arkansas drivers may text while driving?
choices: No driver; texting is not allowed at any age
explanation: Texting while driving is illegal for every Arkansas driver, regardless of age.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 16

prompt: A 17-year-old Arkansas driver may use a cell phone while driving:
choices: For calls but not for texts
explanation: Drivers under 18 may not use a cell phone at all while driving, and hands-free devices are not allowed either. The only exception is an emergency.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 58

prompt: A 19-year-old Arkansas driver wants to make a phone call while driving. What does the law allow?
choices: No phone use at all, even hands-free
Hands-free only; a hand-held phone only in an emergency
explanation: Drivers 18 to 20 may use a hands-free device to talk. A hand-held phone may be used only in an emergency.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 16

prompt: An adult drives past an Arkansas school zone during school hours while children are outside. When may the driver use a hand-held phone?
choices: Anytime, because the driver is over 21
Only for calls under one minute
explanation: No driver may use a hand-held wireless device while passing a school building or school zone during school hours when children are present, except in an emergency.
ref: Arkansas Code Annotated, A.C.A. § 27-51-1605

prompt: In an Arkansas highway work zone while workers are present, holding your phone to take a call while driving is:
choices: A moving traffic violation, and work-zone fines are doubled when workers are present
Allowed if you stay in the right lane
explanation: With highway workers present, no driver may use a hand-held wireless device in a work zone except in an emergency. The study guide counts holding your phone as a moving violation, and work-zone fines are doubled.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 31; A.C.A. § 27-51-1606

prompt: Under Arkansas's seat belt law, who must wear a safety belt?
explanation: Arkansas law makes it illegal to drive or ride as a front-seat passenger without wearing a safety belt.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 21

prompt: Can an Arkansas officer stop you only because the driver or front-seat passenger is not buckled up?
choices: Yes, it is a primary violation
explanation: Since June 30, 2009, Arkansas allows a traffic stop based only on a seat belt violation by the driver or front-seat passenger.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 21

prompt: In Arkansas, a child must ride in a child passenger safety seat if the child is:
choices: Under 8 years old and under 80 pounds
Under 6 years old and under 60 pounds
Under 4 years old and under 40 pounds
Under 2 years old, regardless of weight
explanation: A child under 6 who weighs less than 60 pounds must be in a child passenger safety seat properly secured to the vehicle.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 21

prompt: Arkansas requires all children under what age to wear appropriate safety restraints while the vehicle is moving?
explanation: All children under 15 must wear appropriate safety restraints; those under 6 and under 60 pounds need a child safety seat.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 21

prompt: Arkansas law forbids smoking tobacco in a vehicle when a passenger is younger than:
explanation: A person may not knowingly smoke tobacco in a motor vehicle carrying a child under 14.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 21

prompt: When the driver holds an Arkansas Instruction Permit, which passengers must wear seat belts?
choices: None, if the supervising adult is buckled
explanation: All passengers riding with an Instruction Permit driver must wear seat belts (the same applies to Learner's and Intermediate licenses).
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 15

prompt: What is the minimum age to apply for an Arkansas Instruction Permit?
explanation: You must be at least 14 and pass the knowledge exam and vision test to get an Instruction Permit.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 15

prompt: An Arkansas Instruction Permit holder may practice driving only with:
choices: A licensed driver 21 or older sitting in the seat beside the driver
A parent sitting in the back seat
A licensed driver 25 or older anywhere in the car
explanation: A permit holder may drive with a licensed driver who is 21 or older and occupies the seat beside the driver.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 15

prompt: How long is an Arkansas Instruction Permit valid?
choices: 2 years from the date the knowledge exam was passed
explanation: The permit is issued for two years from the date of the passed knowledge exam, and it cannot be renewed.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, pp. 15, 98

prompt: A 15-year-old with an Arkansas Learner's License may drive only when:
choices: Accompanied by any licensed driver 18 or older
Accompanied by a licensed driver who is at least 21
Driving alone to and from school
explanation: A Learner's License driver must be accompanied by a licensed driver at least 21 years old, and all passengers must wear seat belts.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 15

prompt: To receive an Arkansas Learner's License, the applicant must have had no traffic crash or serious traffic conviction within the previous:
explanation: The applicant cannot be involved in any traffic crash or convicted of a serious traffic violation within the six months before applying.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 15

prompt: At what age can an Arkansas teen get an Intermediate License?
explanation: The Intermediate License is a restricted license issued to drivers between 16 and 18.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 15

prompt: An Arkansas Intermediate License holder may not drive during which hours unless an exception applies?
explanation: Intermediate License drivers may not drive between 11 p.m. and 4 a.m. unless accompanied by a licensed driver 21 or older, driving to or from a school activity, church-related activity or job, or driving because of an emergency.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 16; A.C.A. § 27-16-804

prompt: Without a licensed driver 21 or older in the front seat, how many unrelated minor passengers may an Arkansas Intermediate License holder carry?
explanation: An Intermediate License driver may not carry more than one unrelated minor passenger unless a licensed driver 21 or older is in the front seat.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 16

prompt: Under Arkansas's Intermediate License rules, which passenger counts as an "unrelated minor passenger"?
choices: A child who lives in the driver's household
explanation: An unrelated minor passenger is anyone under 21 who is not the driver's sibling, stepsibling, or a child living in the same household.
ref: Arkansas Code Annotated, A.C.A. § 27-16-804

prompt: Under Arkansas graduated licensing, at what age does a driver normally qualify for the non-restricted Class D license?
explanation: The Class D License is the non-restricted license issued to drivers 18 or older. Younger teens hold a Learner's License (14-15) or an Intermediate License (16-17).
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 16

prompt: After becoming an Arkansas resident, how soon must you get an Arkansas driver's license?
explanation: A new resident must obtain an Arkansas license within 30 calendar days. A nonresident physically present for 6 months must also get one.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 14

prompt: What minimum uncorrected vision is required for an unrestricted Arkansas driver's license?
explanation: An unrestricted license requires uncorrected visual acuity of at least 20/40. With corrective lenses, at least 20/70 is required for a restricted license.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 17

prompt: What does a "B" restriction on an Arkansas driver's license mean?
choices: You must wear your corrective lenses (eyewear) when driving
explanation: A B restriction means you must drive with your glasses or contacts; you can be ticketed for failing to wear them.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 83

prompt: Under Act 1289 of 2015, what fee is charged for each Arkansas written driver exam?
explanation: A $5.00 fee is charged for each written exam, added to the cost of your license and collected by DFA.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 13

prompt: If you fail the Arkansas knowledge test for a learner's permit or license, how long must you wait before retesting?
explanation: Arkansas State Police rules require a 5-calendar-day waiting period before you may retake a failed knowledge test.
ref: Arkansas State Police Non-Commercial Driver's License Testing Rules, Rule 1

prompt: What are Arkansas's minimum liability insurance limits?
explanation: Arkansas requires at least $25,000 for injury or death of one person, $50,000 for two or more people, and $25,000 for property damage in one accident.
ref: Arkansas Code Annotated, A.C.A. § 27-22-104(b)

prompt: When an officer asks during an Arkansas traffic stop, the law requires you to provide:
choices: Your driver's license, proof of insurance, and vehicle registration
Your license and Social Security card
explanation: Arkansas law requires you to provide your driver's license, proof of insurance and vehicle registration when an officer requests them.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 3

prompt: Under Arkansas's point system, a warning letter is mailed when a driver's record reaches:
explanation: Moving violations carry 3 to 8 points. Reaching 10 points triggers a warning letter; 14 or more points brings an automatic hearing.
ref: Arkansas DFA Office of Driver Services, Driver Improvements (Points System)

prompt: In Arkansas, what happens when a driver reaches 14 or more points?
choices: The license is revoked for life
Only a warning letter is sent
explanation: At 14 or more points a hearing is automatically scheduled, which can lead to probation or suspension. Missing the hearing means automatic suspension.
ref: Arkansas DFA Office of Driver Services, Driver Improvements (Points System)

prompt: Who must come with you to your Arkansas driving skills test?
choices: A valid licensed driver age 21 or older
explanation: Bring your instruction permit, a valid licensed driver 21 or older, current proof of insurance and vehicle registration.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 97

prompt: On the Arkansas skills test, you make a second rolling stop after the examiner warned you about the first. What happens?
choices: You fail and receive a two-week penalty before retesting
You lose points but still pass
You must retake the knowledge test
explanation: Two missed attempts in the same category fail the exam. The examiner warns you on the first rolling stop; a second one brings a two-week penalty.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 97

prompt: Your car will be turned away from the Arkansas skills test if its front window tint is darker than:
explanation: Tint darker than 25% on the front windows (or 10% on the back) will be denied, and no tint is allowed on the front windshield.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 98

prompt: In Arkansas, school buses are required to stop at:
explanation: School buses are required to stop at all railroad crossings, so expect a bus ahead of you to stop.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 40

prompt: You are crossing railroad tracks when the crossing gates begin to come down. What does the Arkansas study guide say to do?
choices: Stop on the tracks and back up
Keep going, even if it means you will break the gate
explanation: If the gates begin to come down as you begin to cross, keep going even if it means breaking the gate. Never stop on the tracks.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 41

prompt: When a train is approaching a crossing, where must you stop in Arkansas?
choices: Within 100 feet but not less than 25 feet from the nearest rail
Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
Within 30 feet but not less than 10 feet from the nearest rail
At least 5 feet from the nearest rail
explanation: When a signal, lowered gate, flagger or approaching train requires a stop, stop within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
ref: Arkansas Code Annotated, A.C.A. § 27-51-702

prompt: What do flashing green lights on an Arkansas construction or maintenance vehicle mean?
choices: An active work zone: slow down and use caution
The vehicle is a funeral escort
Traffic may proceed at full speed
explanation: Arkansas authorized flashing green lights on construction and maintenance vehicles. They mark an active work zone, so slow down and use caution.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 30

prompt: You get a speeding ticket in an Arkansas work zone while workers are present. The fine is:
explanation: Any moving violation in a work zone with workers present costs double the fine, which can reach $5,000.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 31

prompt: An ARDOT crew is painting stripes while moving slowly (a mobile work zone). Do Arkansas's doubled work-zone fines apply?
choices: No, only in fixed construction zones
Yes, mobile work zones are treated the same as standard work zones
explanation: Mobile work zones count the same as standard work zones, so fines double in both. They are marked by signs on the back of ARDOT vehicles.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 31

prompt: In Arkansas, when may you turn right on a red light?
choices: Without stopping, if no cars are coming
After a complete stop, unless a sign prohibits it
Only when a green arrow is shown
explanation: You may turn right on red after a complete stop and checking for traffic and pedestrians, unless a sign prohibits it.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 37

prompt: In Arkansas, a left turn on a steady red light is allowed only:
choices: From a one-way street onto another one-way street, after a complete stop
From any street, if no traffic is coming
From a two-way street onto a one-way street
explanation: From the left lane of a one-way street, after a complete stop, you may turn left on red into another one-way street unless a sign prohibits it.
ref: Arkansas Code Annotated, A.C.A. § 27-52-107

prompt: On an Arkansas road, you are passing a car traveling in the same direction when it suddenly slows. Who must yield?
explanation: A driver passing a vehicle must yield to the vehicle being passed, even if it is slowing or stopping, because it may be turning left or avoiding a hazard.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 52

prompt: While you are in an Arkansas intersection, you hear a siren and see flashing lights coming toward you. What should you do?
choices: Speed up to stay ahead of it
Drive through the intersection, then pull to the right edge and stop
explanation: If you are in an intersection, drive through it before pulling over to the right edge of the road.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 23

prompt: Unless on official business, how closely may you follow a fire truck answering an alarm in Arkansas?
explanation: Do not follow a fire truck responding to an alarm closer than 500 feet, or park within the block where it has stopped.
ref: Arkansas Code Annotated, A.C.A. § 27-51-902

prompt: On a multilane Arkansas highway, a police car is stopped on the shoulder with its lights on. What does the law require?
choices: Move to the lane farthest from it if possible; if not, slow down
explanation: Move over to the farthest lane away from the stopped vehicle whenever possible; if changing lanes is unsafe or impossible, reduce your speed.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 27

prompt: Arkansas's Move Over law covers which stopped vehicles with flashing lights?
choices: Only police, fire trucks and ambulances
Emergency vehicles plus ARDOT, utility, construction vehicles and tow trucks
explanation: Arkansas expanded the law beyond police, fire and EMS to ARDOT vehicles, utility vehicles, construction vehicles and tow trucks.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 33

prompt: Violating Arkansas's Move Over law can bring a fine of up to $1,000 and a license suspension of up to:
explanation: Violators can be fined up to $1,000, jailed, ordered to do community service, and have their license suspended for up to six months.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 23; A.C.A. § 27-51-310

prompt: A school bus is stopped with red lights flashing on an Arkansas two-lane road, and you are coming from the opposite direction. You must:
choices: Stop until the lights are turned off and the bus moves
Stop only if children are crossing
Keep going, since you are in the other lane
explanation: No matter where you are - same lane, opposing lane or at an intersection - you must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 24

prompt: You are on a four-lane highway divided by a 25-foot grass median. A school bus stops with red lights flashing on the other side. What must you do?
choices: You do not have to stop, but proceed with caution
Stop only if you see children
explanation: Drivers do not have to stop for a bus on the opposite side of a median 20 feet or more wide.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 24; A.C.A. § 27-51-1005

prompt: A school bus stops with flashing red lights on the far side of a four-lane road that has only a narrow painted median (less than 20 feet). What should you do?
choices: Keep going; the bus is on the other side
Stop only if you are in the left lane
Stop; when the median is under 20 feet, all lanes must stop
explanation: The no-stop exception needs a median of 20 feet or more. With a narrower median, all lanes of traffic must stop.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 25

prompt: What is the penalty for passing a stopped school bus with its red lights flashing in Arkansas?
choices: A fine of at least $250 and up to $1,000, and up to 90 days in jail
A warning for a first offense
explanation: Passing a stopped school bus is a misdemeanor with a fine of $250 to $1,000, up to 90 days in jail, or both.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 25

prompt: Under Arkansas law, at least how far back from a stopped school bus with flashing red lights must you stop?
explanation: Drivers meeting or overtaking a stopped school bus from any direction must stop not less than 30 feet before reaching it.
ref: Arkansas Code Annotated, A.C.A. § 27-51-1004

prompt: Under Isaac's Law, a driver who negligently causes a death while illegally passing a stopped school bus in Arkansas faces:
explanation: Isaac's Law makes negligently causing a death while violating the school bus law a Class C felony (negligent homicide).
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 25

prompt: Under the Arkansas study guide, who has absolute right-of-way?
choices: A driver already in a left-turn lane
A pedestrian carrying a white cane or using a guide dog
explanation: Pedestrians with a white cane or guide dog have absolute right-of-way. Do not honk, which could confuse or frighten them.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 47

prompt: You are cruising in the left lane of an Arkansas multilane highway at the speed limit, not passing anyone. Which is true?
choices: This is allowed if you drive the speed limit
It is allowed only at night
This is against the law; the left lane is for passing, except in a few listed cases
It is allowed when traffic is light
explanation: Arkansas law bars driving in the left lane of a multilane highway except to pass, when other lanes are closed or unsafe, or when preparing to exit on the left.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 75

prompt: Which situation allows you to drive in the left lane of an Arkansas multilane highway when you are not passing?
choices: Driving slower than the speed limit
Preparing to exit the highway on the left
explanation: The left-lane exceptions are passing, all other lanes closed for construction, all other lanes unsafe, and preparing to exit on the left.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 75

prompt: How may you use a shared center left-turn lane in Arkansas?
choices: To turn left from a street or driveway and then merge, but not as an acceleration lane
As an acceleration lane to build up speed
To wait for a parking space
explanation: You may use the center turn lane as part of a left turn from a street or driveway to merge into traffic, but never as an acceleration lane.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 44

prompt: According to the Arkansas study guide, you should never pass within what distance of a hill or curve?
explanation: Always expect an oncoming car and never pass within 1/3 mile of a curve or hill.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 74

prompt: What is the maximum speed limit on Arkansas controlled-access highways outside urban areas that have at least four lanes divided by a median?
explanation: The maximum is 75 mph on rural, divided controlled-access highways with at least four lanes (70 mph for commercial motor vehicles), where posted.
ref: Arkansas Code Annotated, A.C.A. § 27-51-201

prompt: Under Arkansas law, when may you stop on the shoulder or median of an interstate?
choices: Only briefly for an emergency, a disabled vehicle, or to correct an unsafe condition
explanation: Stopping or parking on interstate shoulders, medians and ramps is prohibited except in designated areas or briefly for an emergency, a breakdown, or an unsafe condition.
ref: Arkansas Code Annotated, A.C.A. § 27-51-1302

prompt: When passing a bicycle in Arkansas, you must leave at least:
explanation: Pass a bicycle on the left at a safe distance of not less than 3 feet, and don't move back until safely clear.
ref: Arkansas Code Annotated, A.C.A. § 27-51-311

prompt: In Arkansas, a red or orange pennant flag on a bicycle means:
choices: The rider is in a race
The rider has impaired hearing, so slow down
explanation: A red or orange pennant flag on a bike indicates the rider has impaired hearing. Slow down.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 80

prompt: According to the Arkansas study guide, a car can disappear in a tractor-trailer's blind spot up to how far behind the truck?
explanation: A car can disappear up to 20 feet in front of the cab, along either side, and up to 200 feet behind the truck.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 77

prompt: How much following distance does the Arkansas study guide recommend behind a motorcycle?
explanation: Allow at least 4 to 6 seconds behind a motorcycle so the rider has time to maneuver or stop.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 82

prompt: Under Arkansas law, a bicyclist facing a steady red light may:
choices: Proceed with caution after a complete stop and yielding to traffic that is an immediate hazard
Never proceed until the light turns green
Proceed only when a car is also turning
explanation: Arkansas lets a cyclist go through a steady red after a complete stop and yielding to oncoming traffic that is an immediate hazard, so watch for bikes at red lights.
ref: Arkansas Code Annotated, A.C.A. § 27-51-1803

prompt: What is the Arkansas speed limit when passing a school zone during school hours while children are present?
explanation: The limit is 25 mph when passing a school building or zone during school hours with children present and outside.
ref: Arkansas Code Annotated, A.C.A. § 27-51-212

prompt: If a county judge has not set a speed limit on an Arkansas county road, the limit is:
explanation: When no limit has been set by the county judge, the speed limit on a county road is 40 mph.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 38

prompt: Unless a different limit is posted, what is the maximum speed in an Arkansas urban district?
explanation: Arkansas law sets a 30 mph maximum in any urban district unless a different limit is posted.
ref: Arkansas Code Annotated, A.C.A. § 27-51-201

prompt: You are driving exactly the posted speed limit on an icy Arkansas road. Can you get a ticket?
choices: Yes, you can be ticketed for driving too fast for conditions
No, you are at the limit
explanation: Speed limits are for ideal conditions. Even at the speed limit you can be ticketed for traveling too fast for conditions.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 70

prompt: Several cars have backed up behind your slow-moving vehicle on an Arkansas highway. What should you do?
choices: Keep going; driving slowly is always safe
Turn on hazard lights and keep driving
Pull over and let them pass
explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be as bad as speeding. If vehicles build up behind you, pull over and let them pass.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 68

prompt: Which following-distance rule does the Arkansas study guide teach for normal conditions?
explanation: Use the two-second rule; in some situations, such as slippery roads or poor visibility, use four seconds.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 71

prompt: If rain or fog keeps you from seeing more than 200 feet ahead, the Arkansas study guide says not to drive faster than:
explanation: If you cannot see more than 200 feet ahead in rain or fog, do not drive faster than 30 mph.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 70

prompt: In Arkansas, headlights must be on from:
choices: 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise
1 hour after sunset to 1 hour before sunrise
explanation: Turn on headlights a half hour after sunset until a half hour before sunrise, and any time you cannot see clearly within 500 feet.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 63

prompt: Arkansas law requires your headlights to be on whenever:
explanation: Arkansas law requires drivers to turn on their headlights when windshield wipers are needed.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 63

prompt: Is it legal in Arkansas to drive with only your parking lights on at dusk?
choices: Yes, until it is fully dark
No, driving with only parking lights is illegal
explanation: Parking lights are for parked cars. It is illegal in Arkansas to drive using only parking lights.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 63

prompt: In Arkansas, you must dim your high beams when you come within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle?
explanation: Dim your high beams whenever you come within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 63

prompt: In Arkansas, use your low beams when following another vehicle closer than:
explanation: Use low beams when following another vehicle closer than 200 feet.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 63

prompt: In Arkansas, you may not park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?
explanation: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 54

prompt: In Arkansas, you may not park within how many feet of a crosswalk at an intersection?
explanation: Do not park within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 54

prompt: In Arkansas, you may not park within how many feet of a traffic signal, stop sign, or yield sign?
explanation: Do not park within 30 feet of a traffic signal, stop sign, or yield sign.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 54

prompt: In Arkansas, you may not park within how many feet of a railroad crossing?
explanation: Do not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing, and never park on the tracks.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 54

prompt: In Arkansas, you may not park within how many feet of a fire station driveway on the same side of the street?
explanation: Do not park within 20 feet of a fire station driveway on the same side of the street (or where signs are posted).
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 54

prompt: When parallel parking in Arkansas, your vehicle should be no more than how far from the curb?
explanation: Park 18 inches or less from the curb; parking more than 18 inches away is not allowed.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 53

prompt: In Arkansas, a red-painted curb means:
explanation: A red curb means fire zone; a yellow curb means a loading zone or other restriction.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 54

prompt: After an Arkansas crash in which someone is injured, when must the driver notify the police?
choices: Only if the other driver asks for a report
explanation: When anyone is injured or killed in a crash, the driver must notify police immediately and may not leave the scene until police have the information they need. The 30-day deadline is for the separate written accident report.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 92; A.C.A. § 27-53-202

prompt: When a written accident report is required in Arkansas, it must be filed with the Office of Driver Services within:
explanation: A required accident report must be filed with the DFA Office of Driver Services within 30 days of the crash; someone may file for you if you are injured.
ref: Arkansas Driver License Study Guide, p. 93; A.C.A. § 27-19-501

prompt: Your car is involved in a minor crash in Arkansas and can still be driven. What does Arkansas law say you should do?
choices: Leave it where it stopped until police arrive
Move it off the roadway so it does not block traffic
Drive home and report it later
